prereq.description: Prerequisite relationship between concepts or topics

nodes.name: Bits and Bytes
nodes.description: Information encoded as bit patterns grouped into bytes, with hexadecimal notation used as a compact human-readable representation of the underlying binary machine state.

nodes.name: Integer Representation
nodes.description: How fixed-width integers are encoded in hardware, using unsigned binary for non-negative values and two's complement for signed values, determining the representable ranges.

nodes.name: Integer Arithmetic
nodes.description: Addition, subtraction, and multiplication on fixed-width integers, including modular wraparound and overflow that follow from finite two's-complement and unsigned encodings.

nodes.name: Floating Point Representation
nodes.description: The IEEE 754 standard encoding real numbers as sign, biased exponent, and fraction fields, supporting normalised, denormalised, infinity, and NaN values.

nodes.name: Floating Point Operations
nodes.description: Arithmetic on IEEE 754 values, where results are rounded to representable numbers, making operations non-associative and introducing rounding error and special-case behaviour.

nodes.name: x86-64 Data Movement
nodes.description: x86-64 instructions that move data between registers and memory, using addressing modes and operand sizes to load, store, and copy machine words.

nodes.name: Arithmetic and Logical Operations
nodes.description: x86-64 instructions performing integer arithmetic, bitwise logic, and shifts on registers and memory, updating condition-code flags used by later conditional instructions.

nodes.name: Control Flow (Conditionals and Loops)
nodes.description: Implementing conditionals and loops in assembly using condition-code flags, conditional jumps, and comparison instructions to direct the processor's instruction stream.

nodes.name: Procedures and Call Stack
nodes.description: How procedures are called using the runtime stack to pass arguments, save return addresses, allocate local storage, and follow register-saving conventions.

nodes.name: Arrays and Structs
nodes.description: The memory layout of arrays and structures, including element addressing arithmetic, field offsets, and alignment requirements imposed by the architecture.

nodes.name: Instruction Set Architecture (Y86-64)
nodes.description: The Y86-64 instruction set, a simplified teaching ISA defining registers, instruction encodings, and semantics used to study processor implementation.

nodes.name: Sequential CPU Implementation
nodes.description: A sequential processor design executing each instruction through fetch, decode, execute, memory, and write-back stages within a single clock cycle.

nodes.name: Pipelining Principles
nodes.description: Overlapping the execution of multiple instructions across pipeline stages to increase instruction throughput, ideally completing one instruction per clock cycle.

nodes.name: Pipeline Hazards and Forwarding
nodes.description: Data, control, and structural hazards that stall pipelines, and forwarding techniques that resolve data dependencies without waiting for write-back.

nodes.name: Exceptions in Pipelines
nodes.description: Handling exceptions in a pipelined processor, requiring precise state by detecting events in order and squashing partially executed younger instructions.

nodes.name: Compiler Limitations
nodes.description: Reasons compilers cannot fully optimise code, including memory aliasing, function side effects, and conservative assumptions that block otherwise valid transformations.

nodes.name: Loop Unrolling
nodes.description: An optimisation that replicates loop bodies to reduce loop-control overhead and expose more independent instructions for instruction-level parallelism.

nodes.name: Instruction-Level Parallelism
nodes.description: Executing independent instructions simultaneously on superscalar, pipelined hardware, limited by data dependencies and the processor's functional-unit latency and throughput.

nodes.name: Memory Aliasing
nodes.description: When two pointers may reference the same memory location, forcing the compiler to preserve memory accesses and preventing certain optimisations.

nodes.name: Profiling Tools
nodes.description: Tools that measure where a program spends time, identifying performance bottlenecks so optimisation effort targets the most costly code paths.

nodes.name: Storage Technologies
nodes.description: Characteristics and trends of storage technologies such as SRAM, DRAM, disks, and SSDs, differing in speed, capacity, volatility, and cost per byte.

nodes.name: Principle of Locality
nodes.description: Programs tend to reuse recently accessed data (temporal locality) and nearby data (spatial locality), a behaviour that caching exploits to improve performance.

nodes.name: Cache Memory Organization
nodes.description: How caches are organised into sets, lines, and blocks with tags, governing the placement, lookup, and replacement of cached memory blocks.

nodes.name: Cache Performance Metrics
nodes.description: Metrics such as hit rate, miss rate, miss penalty, and average memory access time used to evaluate cache effectiveness.

nodes.name: Writing Cache-Friendly Code
nodes.description: Structuring data access patterns to maximise temporal and spatial locality, improving cache hit rates and overall program performance.

nodes.name: Static Linking
nodes.description: Combining relocatable object files at build time into a single executable by resolving symbols and merging sections into the final image.

nodes.name: Object Files (ELF)
nodes.description: The Executable and Linkable Format that structures object files into sections and symbol tables used by linkers and loaders.

nodes.name: Symbol Resolution
nodes.description: The linker step associating each symbol reference with exactly one symbol definition across object files and libraries, detecting duplicates.

nodes.name: Relocation
nodes.description: The linker step that assigns final run-time addresses to merged sections and patches symbol references to point at those addresses.

nodes.name: Dynamic Linking
nodes.description: Deferring symbol resolution to load or run time by linking against shared libraries, reducing executable size and enabling code sharing.

nodes.name: Exceptions (Traps, Interrupts, Faults)
nodes.description: Abrupt changes in control flow triggered by events, classified as traps, interrupts, faults, and aborts, that transfer control to the kernel.

nodes.name: Processes and Context Switches
nodes.description: The process abstraction giving each program a private address space and logical control flow, switched by the kernel saving and restoring context.

nodes.name: Process Control (fork, execve)
nodes.description: System calls that create processes with fork, load new programs with execve, and reap children with wait, managing the process lifecycle.

nodes.name: Signals and Signal Handling
nodes.description: A mechanism delivering asynchronous notifications to processes, with handlers that interrupt normal control flow to respond to events.

nodes.name: Non-local Jumps
nodes.description: Transferring control across function boundaries using setjmp and longjmp, bypassing the normal call-return discipline for error recovery.

nodes.name: Address Translation
nodes.description: Hardware mapping of virtual addresses to physical addresses via the MMU and page tables, giving each process its own address space.

nodes.name: Page Tables
nodes.description: Multi-level data structures mapping virtual pages to physical frames, storing permission and presence bits used during address translation.

nodes.name: Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)
nodes.description: A small hardware cache of recent virtual-to-physical translations that accelerates address translation by avoiding repeated page-table walks.

nodes.name: Dynamic Memory Allocation
nodes.description: Managing heap memory at run time with allocators like malloc and free, balancing throughput, fragmentation, and memory utilisation.

nodes.name: Garbage Collection Basics
nodes.description: Automatic reclamation of unreachable heap memory by tracing or counting references, freeing the programmer from explicit deallocation.

nodes.name: Unix I/O
nodes.description: The Unix model treating files, devices, and sockets uniformly through descriptors and the open, read, write, and close system calls.

nodes.name: File Metadata
nodes.description: Information about a file stored separately from its contents, such as size, permissions, and timestamps, accessed via the stat system call.

nodes.name: Standard I/O Library
nodes.description: A buffered, portable I/O library layered over Unix system calls that reduces system-call overhead through stream buffering.

nodes.name: File Sharing
nodes.description: How descriptors, open-file table entries, and inodes interact so processes can share open files and offsets, especially after fork.

nodes.name: I/O Redirection
nodes.description: Redirecting a process's standard input or output to files using dup2 to duplicate descriptors onto the standard descriptor numbers.

nodes.name: Client-Server Model
nodes.description: A networking model where client processes request services and server processes provide them, communicating over a transport-layer connection.

nodes.name: Internet Protocol (IP)
nodes.description: The network-layer protocol providing best-effort, connectionless delivery of packets across interconnected networks using hierarchical IP addressing.

nodes.name: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)
nodes.description: The transport protocol providing reliable, ordered, connection-oriented byte streams over IP using acknowledgements, retransmission, and flow control.

nodes.name: Sockets Interface
nodes.description: The API for network programming that abstracts connections as file descriptors, with calls such as socket, bind, listen, connect, and accept.

nodes.name: HTTP Protocol Basics
nodes.description: The application-layer request-response protocol underlying the web, using methods, headers, and status codes to transfer resources over TCP.

nodes.name: Thread Basics
nodes.description: Threads as independent logical flows sharing a process's address space, created and joined to achieve concurrency within a single process.

nodes.name: Shared Variables
nodes.description: How threads share global and heap variables, and the memory model determining when one thread's writes become visible to others.

nodes.name: Synchronization (Semaphores)
nodes.description: Coordinating threads using semaphores, counting primitives whose P and V operations enforce mutual exclusion and scheduling constraints.

nodes.name: Thread Safety
nodes.description: Properties making functions safe to call concurrently, including reentrancy and avoiding unsynchronised access to shared mutable state.

nodes.name: Deadlocks
nodes.description: A state where threads are permanently blocked, each waiting for resources held by others, arising when the four Coffman conditions hold.
